demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

vignette: Raj is a 52-year-old South Asian man who works as a maid in a busy downtown hotel. He was married for many years but recently divorced, and he now lives alone in a small apartment near his workplace. Raj's life took an unexpected turn three months ago when he accidentally caused serious injury to another worker at the hotel. It happened on a particularly hectic Friday evening. The floors were slippery from an unnoticed spill, and as Raj was pushing a heavy cleaning cart through one of the hotel's busy hallways, it veered out of control and struck his colleague, Ram. Ram fell hard against the wall and crumpled to the ground, immediately holding his wrist in agony. Raj's heart sank; he knew something terrible had happened. Since that day, Raj has been haunted by what occurred. He wakes up with a start from dreams where he sees Ram lying on the floor, screaming in pain. The images are so vivid and disturbing that they linger throughout the day, causing him to feel constantly anxious and overwhelmed. When he's at work, every creak of the floorboards or any sudden noise makes him jump. He finds himself frequently looking over his shoulder for signs of danger, as if something else is about to go wrong. Raj avoids working in areas where there are slippery surfaces or heavy equipment. The thought of accidentally causing another injury terrifies him. His concentration at work has suffered significantly; he often spaces out and makes small mistakes that weren't part of his usual routine before the accident. He tries to push through these feelings, but they are persistent and exhausting. The incident has also affected his relationships with colleagues. Raj feels immense guilt about what happened to Ram, who is still recovering from a broken wrist. Though other workers have been understanding, Raj finds it hard to interact with them without feeling ashamed. At times, he avoids eye contact and even skips breaks to minimize social interactions. His former closeness with some of his coworkers has faded into awkward silences. At home, Raj often feels isolated and disconnected from others. He no longer participates in community events or gatherings that were once an important part of his life. Instead, he spends much of his free time indoors, engrossed in news about workplace accidents, which only serves to heighten his anxiety further. The news stories are a constant reminder of the vulnerability of his work environment and how easily things can go wrong. Raj's sleep has become erratic and disrupted. He lies awake at night replaying the accident over and over again, wondering if he could have done something differently. His insomnia is compounded by nightmares that leave him drenched in sweat and with a pounding heart. On some mornings, Raj barely makes it to work on time because of his disturbed sleep. Despite these challenges, Raj tries to maintain his focus at work. He takes extra care to avoid any potential hazards and has become overly cautious about every task he performs. This meticulousness can be seen as an adaptive strategy, but it also reflects the ongoing fear and vulnerability that consume him daily. Raj's sense of self-worth has been deeply affected by the incident. He feels like a failure not only because he caused harm to someone else but also because he cannot help but question his ability to manage basic tasks without causing further damage. This internal struggle is evident in his behavior and interactions, making it hard for him to feel secure or confident. Through all of this, Raj remains committed to his job, though the shadow of that one moment continues to loom over everything he does. He carries the weight of guilt and fear with him every day, a constant reminder of how profoundly life can change in an instant.
